elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 7.2 now reads: "Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor, or to match for Vendor, any commercial offer it receives from another provider." The prior disclose-and-match obligation ("Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives") is gone, and Section 12.3 independently confirms Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." No other clause imposes a matching, notice, or best-terms duty on Customer for Vendor's benefit; the right-to-match mechanic that previously made this an MFN running against us has been eliminated rather than merely narrowed.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer MFN at all (Section 7.2 affirmatively negates any disclosure or matching duty), so there is no scope to confine to a defined product. A zero-scope outcome is at least as protective as a product-limited MFN.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer-side MFN or matching obligation survives, so no duration limit is required. Nothing in the rendered 7.2 or 12.3 creates a time-limited or open-ended obligation on Customer.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no obligation to compare or match third-party offers, there is no comparison mechanic requiring like-for-like carve-outs. Section 12.3's acknowledgment of no most-favoured-customer commitment reinforces this.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Duplicate listing of the fallback scope element; same analysis — no Customer MFN remains, so the scope limitation is vacuously satisfied.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the sole preferred element is met because rendered Section 7.2 replaces the disclose-and-match duty with an express statement that Customer owes no disclosure or matching obligation to Vendor, and no residual best-terms, notice, or right-to-match mechanic survives elsewhere.

Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously — their stated condition (an existing Customer MFN) no longer applies once the obligation is removed — so no scope, 12-month, or like-for-like carve-out drafting is needed.

Minimality holds: only the offending sentence in Section 7.2 was changed; the favourable Section 12.3 acknowledgment was left verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures, remedies, or Vendor-side MFN language were added or deleted. Replacing the section with a short negating sentence (rather than deleting the numbering) is a concise, in-scope edit; the mild overlap with Section 12.3's 'no most-favoured-customer commitment' is clarifying rather than a new operative requirement.

Intent is preserved: pricing, term, supplier-engagement freedom, and all other commercial mechanics are untouched; the edit removes the direct contradiction between old Section 7.2 and Section 12.3 and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Deterministic gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with the substantive reading; the deviation classification is correct because the original clause failed every fallback element (no defined product, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs) and sat in walk-away territory.
